Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a run-of-show into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme run-of-show and deliver a live timeline: Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn for 90 guests, three courses
Resource limits: one kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one dance floor.
Everything must be finished by band's last set.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Wedding Reception Run Sheet — Ashgrove Barn, 90 guests

The ceremony breaks at four o'clock and this sheet starts there. One kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, two servers on the floor, one band. The planner owns the room call; the MC owns everything that goes through the microphone. Nothing on the pass overlaps: the kitchen plates one course at a time and the floor waits for it.

Room
Flip the ceremony room to reception seating: 45 minutes, chairs out, rounds in, linen on.
Dress the tables with centrepieces, place cards and candles; 15 minutes once the flip is done.
Seat the guests when the planner calls the room; 15 minutes to get 90 people down.

Foyer
Open the bar as soon as the ceremony breaks; 20 minutes to set and pour the first round.
Pass canapes in the foyer from twenty minutes in, and keep passing for forty minutes to an hour, however long the photographs take.
Call the room to dinner once the canapes are done; 5 minutes.

Kitchen
Starters plate up fifteen minutes after the room starts seating; 15 minutes on the pass.
Mains go on the pass five minutes after the starter plates are cleared; 30 minutes.
Dessert plates up the moment the cake is cut; 15 minutes.

Floor
Serve the starters; 10 minutes.
Clear the starters twenty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the mains; 15 minutes.
Clear the mains forty minutes after they go out; 10 minutes.
Serve the dessert; 10 minutes.

Programme
Welcome toast as soon as the guests are seated; 5 minutes on the microphone.
First dance once the main plates are cleared; 5 minutes.
Speeches when the MC cues them: two or three of them, fifteen minutes total, twenty-five at the outside.
Cut the cake straight after the speeches; 10 minutes.
Dancing starts ten minutes after the dessert is served and runs until the band's last set.

Notes for the day
The photographs are the only thing we do not control, so the canape window is the slack in the sheet: if the couple are late back from the orchard the bar carries it. Everything downstream of the room call is fixed. If the speeches run long, the kitchen holds the dessert rather than plating it early — the pass is the bottleneck and a plated dessert sitting under a lamp is worse than a five minute gap on the floor.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

**Read-back**

This is a wedding reception run sheet for 90 guests at Ashgrove Barn, covering three courses, and it starts on one clock at the moment the ceremony breaks — four o'clock — not at the ceremony itself. Work splits across four parallel crews hanging off that moment: the room (flip the ceremony space to rounds, dress the tables, seat 90 people), the foyer (open the bar and pour a first round, then pass canapes), the kitchen pass (plates starters, then mains, then dessert — one course at a time, never overlapping), and the floor (two servers serving and clearing each course), with the MC’s programme — welcome toast, first dance, speeches, cake cut, then dancing — riding on top of all of it. The single-instance things are the real shape of the day: one kitchen pass, one bar, one microphone, one dance floor, and one band, plus exactly two servers on the floor, so the floor is the second bottleneck after the pass. Two things are explicitly *held* rather than worked early: the dessert is not plated until the cake is cut, and if the speeches run long the kitchen holds it back rather than let a plated dessert sit under a lamp — a five-minute gap on the floor beats that. The only genuine slack in the sheet is the canape window (starting 20 minutes in, lasting 40 to 60 minutes depending on how long the photographs take); everything downstream of the room call is fixed. Two gaps I won’t invent: the sheet says everything must be finished by the band’s last set but never gives a clock time for it, and it never says how many people are in the kitchen or on the room crew (only that there are two servers, one planner and an MC). The speech block is likewise a range, 15 minutes nominal and 25 at the outside.
